$comment: ALTERNATIVE instruction set (test_instructions) for validating prompt-profile customization.
Voice: explain every file to a brand-new engineer. Be concrete, specific, and consistent so any AI reader interprets it the same way.
Only the guidance text, field order, and selected fields differ from the defaults; the output keys and their types are unchanged.
To restore the defaults, copy test_instructions/codedoc.config.default.json over codedoc.config.json.

requested_shape.description: Summarize this file for a developer who has never seen it. In 2 to 4 sentences, state the concrete problem it solves, when or where it runs in the program's lifecycle, and why it exists. Do not restate the file name and do not list imports.
requested_shape.role_in_system: Explain how this file fits the wider architecture: which layer or subsystem it belongs to, what calls into it, and what it calls out to. Name concrete collaborators (modules, classes, functions) when they are visible in the code.
key_concepts: List 2 to 5 specific concepts, algorithms, patterns, or domain terms a reader must already understand to follow this file (for example: atomic file write, topological sort, rate-limit backoff). Prefer precise named terms over generic words like logic or helpers.

functions.name: <function or method defined IN this file>
functions.description: One precise sentence stating what this function does and its key input, return value, or side effect. Describe observable behavior, not the line-by-line implementation.

classes.name: <class defined IN this file>
classes.description: One sentence naming the single responsibility this class owns and the real-world thing or state it models or manages.

exports: Each public name this module is meant to be imported and used by other files; skip private helpers and names that begin with an underscore.

internal: Relative import paths that resolve to other source files inside this same project.
external: Third-party package names installed from a registry (pip, npm, pub, or maven). Do not include standard-library modules here.

catalog_updates.name: <normalized dependency name>
catalog_updates.used_for: One durable, project-level sentence describing what this dependency is used for across the whole codebase (reusable knowledge, not a detail specific to this one file).

usage_notes.used_for: A short note describing how THIS specific file uses the imported item.

requested_shape.usage_example: One realistic single-line example showing how another file would import or call the main thing this file exposes. Use an empty string if nothing here is meant to be imported.

requested_shape.description: In 2 to 3 sentences, describe what this file contains and its overall purpose from a structural standpoint: its main definitions and what they collectively achieve. Do not restate the file name.
requested_shape.role_in_system: State where this file sits in the codebase and how the symbols it defines are meant to be used by other parts of the system.

functions.name: <function or method defined IN this file>
functions.description: One clear sentence describing what this function does, focused on its observable behavior and its inputs and outputs.

classes.name: <class defined IN this file>
classes.description: One sentence describing the class's responsibility and the state or concept it encapsulates.

catalog_updates.name: <normalized dependency name>
catalog_updates.used_for: One durable, project-level sentence describing what this dependency is used for across the whole codebase.

requested_shape.description: Write a thorough, self-contained paragraph a new team member could read to fully understand this file: the problem it solves, how it works at a high level, and why it exists. Do not restate the file name and do not dump imports.
